title: The boy at twelve, the flyer's crab
logline: Gully's son at twelve at the counter with a pencil, drawing a crab on scrap, from behind — the twenty-ninth flyer's crab, five months early, practicing. His sister's tin beside him. The page can see it's better than the first one.

panels.composition: A boy of twelve from behind at a shop counter drawing a crab in pencil on scrap paper, a pushpin tin beside him, the corkboard above.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a boy of twelve seen from behind at a shop counter drawing a crab in pencil on scrap paper with a pushpin tin beside him, a crowded corkboard above, no words legible

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run

notes: Practicing. Better than the first one.
